title: Mac user caught by the 90-day expiry with no warning

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

input.subject: Password not accepted on anything since this morning

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
Since I opened the laptop this morning nothing takes my password. Mail,
Teams, the build server, all of it says the password is wrong. It is the same
password I have used since June and I have not changed it.

I did not get any warning that it was about to expire.

Aisha

must_include.what: Send her to the self-service reset at aka.ms/sspr
State the new password rules: at least 14 characters, not one of the last 5

must_not_include.what: Treats it as a lockout and tells her to wait for the window to clear
Claims she was warned 14 days beforehand; macOS does not show that warning

characteristics: Two or three steps; the cause is known, so no diagnosis
Explains that macOS does not show the expiry warning, which is why it was a surprise

rationale: Ninety days after June is the expiry window, and the runbook's own note says the 14-day warning appears on Windows sign-in but not on macOS - which is why Mac users are the ones caught out. She cannot sign in to anything and has no workaround, so P2 (G1). A password that expired on schedule is a control working, not an exposure, so not security-sensitive (G3). The lockout runbook shares every word of her symptom and would send her off to wait out a window that is not running (G10).
